rationale: In ⲟⲩⲛⲁⲅ ⲧⲟⲛϣ ⲉⲛ ⲡⲉ ⲡⲉⲥⲣⲉϣⲉ ('her joy is no great slightness') the negated construction requires a noun for smallness/feebleness. Likely from Sahidic ⲧⲱⲛⲉϥ 'be feeble, faint' (Crum 422a) substantivized.

proposed_english: to put forth as teaching / bring forth as instruction
rationale: Compound on ϩⲁⲧ ('front, fore' = ϩⲏⲧ⸗) + ⲥⲃⲱ ('teaching'), giving 'bring-forth-as-teaching.' Parallels ⲭⲡⲟ 'beget' in this kephalaion's parable of wisdom-birthing. Used here in causative ⲉⲧⲣⲉϥ-ϩⲁⲧⲥⲃⲱ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲥ for the man bringing wisdom forth from his heart as teaching.

Verbal-noun pair: as substantive 'beauty/comeliness' (ⲡⲉⲥⲁⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲧⲉ 'her beauty,' line 25); as verb 'grow beautiful, become more comely' in habitual ϣⲁⲥ-/ϣⲁϩ- (lines 24, 27). Built on ⲥⲁⲓⲉ 'beauty' + Lyc. extending suffix -ⲉⲩⲧⲉ (cf. ⲁⲓⲉⲩⲧⲉ 'extend, become long').

Greek loanword, likely συναίσθησις 'sense-perception, awareness' with Lyc. orthographic adaptation. Listed alongside thought and sight as the comprehensive third element of the mother's response to her newborn.
Greek loanword τέρψις 'delight, enjoyment.' Standard Greek philosophical/aesthetic term, distinct from ⲣⲉϣⲉ 'joy' in the same passage.

proposed_english: the watching of the eyes / the gaze
rationale: In line 12 the abstract verbal-noun ⲓ̈ⲱⲣϩ (cf. glossary ⲡⲓ̈ⲱⲣϩ 'the watcher') governs ⲛⲃⲉⲗ 'eyes' as 'the seeing-faculty of his eyes' — what is hidden during pregnancy and emerges at birth.
